critique.good: All eight headers resolve to three lines, so the header band is as short as the 527px budget allows; data cells stay on one line and no numeric or identifier token is broken. The table is compact and easy to scan row by row.
critique.problems: The width distribution is uneven. Columns 4 and 6 are 73px wide although their data are only 1–3 digits and their 8-character headers still need three lines; column 7, which holds two-digit alert counts, is only 63px. The nine-character headers in columns 1 and 8 are also tight at 66px and 63px. The extra white space in columns 4 and 6 breaks the horizontal rhythm and gives the quantitative columns unequal emphasis.
critique.cause: At 73px, columns 4 and 6 have 52px of text width, still short of the roughly 53px needed for four Chinese characters per line, so they remain three lines. The extra 11px only adds empty space. Meanwhile column 7 and the two nine-character headers stay at the three-character minimum.

critique.good: The 84px identifier column creates a clear separate zone for the row header, and columns 4, 6 and 7 at 68px keep their headers to three lines. Data cells remain intact.
critique.problems: Columns 2, 3 and 5 at 58px drop to two characters per line and become four-line headers, making the header band 94px tall. Column 1 at 84px wraps 4/4/1, leaving an orphaned “号” on the last line. The table feels top-heavy and rhythmically uneven.
critique.cause: At 58px the text width is only 37px, below the roughly 41px needed for three Chinese characters per line, so those headers need four lines. At 84px column 1 has 63px of text width, enough for four characters but not five, so the nine-character identifier header breaks 4/4/1. The fixed total width then starves the binary columns.

critique.good: Columns 4, 6 and 7 at 80px give clean two-line headers such as “日志留存/天数达标”, “高危端口/关闭数量” and “近三十天/告警次数”, and the numeric columns are comfortable.
critique.problems: Column 8 at 57px collapses to two characters per line and a five-line header ending in a lone “况”. Columns 2, 3 and 5 at 56px are four lines. The header band is 114px tall and the table 314px, with the two-line numeric headers sitting in a much taller band with empty space. The table looks unbalanced and wastes vertical space.
critique.cause: At 57px the text width is 36px, below the roughly 41px threshold for three characters per line, so the nine-character emergency-contact header needs five lines. At 56px the binary columns are forced to two characters per line. The 80px given to columns 4, 6 and 7 is more than the roughly 74px needed for two lines, draining width from column 8.

critique.good: Perfectly regular 8-column grid; no column is favored, all data cells stay on one line, and the vertical rhythm is calm. 是/否 values and numbers are easy to compare because the columns are identical.
critique.problems: The header is a solid three-line wall: every label has the same visual weight. Binary 是/否 columns are as wide as quantitative columns, while 180/365/30 sit in cramped columns. The row identifier does not read as a row header. Several headers split compounds awkwardly: 系统账/户口令/强度, 外部网/络访问/开放, 日志留/存天数/达标.
critique.cause: 66–65px leaves only 44–45px of text, enough for three CJK characters but not four. Every 8–9-character header therefore wraps to three lines; no column reaches 75px for four characters or 88px for five, so no header can become two lines and no hierarchy is possible.

critique.good: The slight widening of col1 and the quantitative columns shows an attempt to differentiate roles; the grid remains stable, all data stays intact, and no cells are split mid-word.
critique.problems: The differences are too small to read as hierarchy; the table looks almost equal but slightly arbitrary. All headers still wrap to three lines, so the extra pixels buy no cleaner breaks. Col1 at 70px and col4 at 67px still split compounds such as 服务器 and 留存.
critique.cause: 63–70px gives 42–49px of text, still inside the three-character band: about 40px fits, but 53.5px does not. Only 75px allows four characters. The 3–7px changes never cross that threshold, so they add irregularity without reflow.

critique.good: Best of the three: 75px on cols 4 and 7 crosses the four-character threshold, so 日志留存/天数达标 and 近三十天/告警次数 become clean two-line headers. The quantitative columns gain air, and the two-line headers are spaced apart, giving a readable rhythm.
critique.problems: Only two columns improve; the other six remain three-line, including the 9-character row identifier and contact headers. The header row stays 73px because the three-line labels still set it, so the two-line headers do not reduce height. Col1 at 64px is barely wider than the binary columns, so 01 does not stand apart; col8 at 64px is cramped. Col6 is left at 63px while cols 4 and 7 get 75px, so the quantitative treatment is uneven.
critique.cause: 75−21=54px just fits four ~13.4px characters; 62–64px gives 41–43px, only three characters. The design applies the 75px threshold only to cols 4 and 7. Col1 and col8 are 9 characters, so two lines would need about 88px for five characters, not 64px; at 64px they can only break 3+3+3, splitting 服务器 and 联系/确认. The remaining 5px above the six 62px minima is spread across col1, col6, and col8 without changing any line count.

critique.good: The two quantitative columns (4 and 7) get 75px, enough for clean 4/4 two-line headers, and every data cell stays on one line. The table remains compact at 273px, with uniform 33px data rows.
critique.problems: The identifier column is badly cramped: 受检服务器唯一编号 breaks as 受检服/务器唯/一编号, splitting 服务器. The last column breaks 应急联系人 as 应急联/系人确/认情况. Header line counts are uneven—two 2-line headers among six 3-line ones—and the extra width is spent on numeric columns whose values need only about 25px.
critique.cause: col1 is 67px, leaving 46px of text width: enough for 3 Chinese characters but not 4, so the 9-character header falls into 3/3/3 and cuts a word. cols 4 and 7 are 75px, leaving 54px: enough for 4 characters, so those headers become 2 lines while the 62px columns stay at 3. The numeric data do not need that extra 13px.

critique.good: The identifier column at 88px lets 受检服务器/唯一编号 break 5/4 at a word boundary, clearly separating the row identifier from the checks. All data cells stay on one line; the middle columns hold 3 characters per header line; the table is compact and rows scan cleanly.
critique.problems: The 8-character check headers split 3/3/2, often cutting compounds: 系统账/户口令/强度, 漏洞补/丁更新/状态. The last column still splits 联系人 as 应急联/系人确/认情况. The header line counts differ—first column 2 lines, the rest 3—so the first header has extra blank space below.
critique.cause: 62px gives 41px of text, enough for 3 Chinese characters but not 4, forcing 8-character headers into 3/3/2. 67px gives 46px, also 3 characters per line, so the 9-character last header becomes 3/3/3. The 88px first column is the minimum that fits a 5-character first line; widening col8 to 89px would require taking 22px from the middle columns, which would force them to 4 lines.

r0A.idea: A balanced grid with near-equal check columns and slight extra width for the three numeric columns, keeping the table visually even and easy to scan.

r0B.idea: A row-header-first layout: a wide identifier column for quick row recognition, compact binary-status columns, and moderate numeric columns.

r0C.idea: A semantic-band layout that squeezes binary columns and gives generous width to days/counts so quantitative values align and compare clearly, accepting taller wrapped headers.

r1A.idea: Even out r0A: remove the arbitrary extra width from columns 4 and 6, give it to column 7 and the tight emergency-contact header, and keep every header at three lines. Columns 1–7 get 66px and column 8 gets 65px, so all text blocks have enough room for three Chinese characters per line without creating four- or five-line headers.

r1B.idea: Make column roles explicit without increasing header height. Column 1 gets 70px for the nine-character row identifier; binary status columns 2, 3 and 5 get the safe 63px minimum; quantitative columns 4, 6 and 7 get 67px; column 8 gets 67px for its nine-character confirmation header. All headers remain three lines.

r1C.idea: Test controlled two-line headers in the quantitative columns. Columns 4 and 7 get 75px so their eight-character headers break as 4+4 (“日志留存/天数达标”, “近三十天/告警次数”), while columns 1 and 8 stay at 64px and columns 2, 3, 5 and 6 stay at 62–63px so no column exceeds three lines. This avoids r0C’s five-line column 8 while giving the key numeric columns cleaner phrase breaks.

r2A.idea: Refine r1C: keep the two 75px quantitative headers, cols 4 and 7, that produce clean 4+4 breaks, but move the 5px of slack above the six 62px minima into col1 at 67px. This makes the row identifier visibly wider than the binary columns without crossing the 75px point that would create a 4+4+1 orphan in its 9-character header. Col8 returns to 62px, which still holds three characters per line. Sum 527px; all data cells remain one line.

r2B.idea: New alternative: spend width on the 9-character row identifier instead of the quantitative headers. At 88px, 受检服务器唯一编号 breaks cleanly as 受检服务器 / 唯一编号 on two lines, and col8 gets 67px to avoid a 4+4+1 orphan while keeping its header at three lines. All six 8-character check headers stay at 62px and wrap 3+3+2. This sacrifices the two two-line quantitative headers to test whether a strong first-column anchor is worth more. Sum 527px.

r3A.idea: Keep col1 at 88px for 受检服务器/唯一编号. Narrow cols 2–6 to 55px so each 8-character header breaks into four intact 2-character words (系统/账户/口令/强度, 外部/网络/访问/开放, etc.) instead of 3/3/2 fragments. Give col7 75px for 近三十天/告警次数 and col8 89px for 应急联系人/确认情况. This adds one header line but preserves every header word and creates a clear identifier / five-check block / alert-and-contact grouping; all data still fits on one line. Sum = 527px.

understanding.purpose: A server security baseline audit record: six servers checked against multiple compliance items, intended for verification, comparison, and sign-off.
understanding.reading: Readers identify a server by the first column, then scan across its status and numeric checks; binary results are compared vertically, while days and counts are compared as quantities.
groups: Column 1 is the row identifier and should stand apart from the check columns.
Columns 2, 3, 5, and 8 are binary compliance/confirmation statuses (是/否) and can share narrow widths.
Columns 4, 6, and 7 are quantitative measures (days, port count, alert count) and benefit from extra width for numeric alignment.
keep_intact: Numeric values such as 180, 90, 365, 30, port counts, and alert counts
Two-character Chinese header terms where possible, avoiding single-character orphans
may_wrap: Long Chinese headers, especially 系统账户口令强度, 外部网络访问开放, 漏洞补丁更新状态, and 应急联系人确认情况
The nine-character identifier and emergency-contact headers may wrap to two or three lines
Data cells should remain on one line

bad.why: Five-line headers create a 114px header band and a 314px table, so the header block dominates the six data rows; the 56–62px columns break 8–9-character labels into two-character fragments.
The 55px middle columns force four-line headers and two-character line fragments, while the 88/89px end columns waste width on two-digit IDs and 是/否 values; the table is both taller and less even.

final.rationale: r2B gives the row-identifier column enough width to break the 9-character label cleanly as 受检服务器 / 唯一编号, while keeping the seven check columns close to equal so the table reads as row labels plus peer checks. At 62px the middle columns still hold every value on one line, and their headers settle into a uniform three-line band, keeping the table compact. r1C/r2A buy two-line headers for columns 4 and 7 but create an arbitrary 3-2-3 rhythm and a cramped first column; r1A/r1B avoid that rhythm but split 服务器/唯一编号 awkwardly. r0C and r3A push too far into narrow middle columns, producing 4–5 line headers and an over-tall header block.

general: Allocate width by header readability when values are short; do not size columns by the widest number if every number already fits.
A row-header column can be wider than the data columns even when its values are tiny, because it carries the row hierarchy.
Unequal widths should map to a semantic role or a real line-break gain; scattered extra widths read as noise.
A consistent header line count often beats a mix of 2- and 3-line headers unless the shorter break preserves a meaningful phrase.
Avoid dropping below roughly three CJK characters of content per line; below that, headers become 4–5 lines and dominate.
specific: Here the 9-character end headers need about 86px for a clean 5+4 break, while the 8-character middle headers need about 73px for a 4+4 break; eight such columns cannot all get that width in 527px.
62px (41px content) is the practical floor for 3 CJK characters per line at 13px; 58px drops to 2 characters and 4 lines.
75px gives 4 characters per line and two-line headers for the 8-character middle labels, which is why r1C/r2A widen columns 4 and 7.
The data are only 01–06, 是/否, and 0–365, so 62px is sufficient for every value; the layout is driven entirely by header wrapping.

final.tradeoffs: One could prefer r1A for a perfectly even grid, or r1C/r2A to give columns 4 and 7 two-line headers, at the cost of a more uneven header rhythm and a narrower first column. r2B's 88px first column is generous for two-digit IDs; a designer who values uniform column rhythm over the clean 受检服务器 / 唯一编号 break would reject it.
final.uncertain: Whether the two-line first header justifies 88px, whether column 8 needs 67px rather than 62px, and how exact break thresholds shift with font metrics and browser line-breaking.

A.why: Columns are near-even, so every header wraps to a consistent three lines and the header band reads as one horizontal unit; all values (180, 365, 11) sit comfortably and rows scan cleanly. Slightly wasteful on col 1, whose IDs are two characters, but nothing breaks or crowds.

B.why: Col 1 is given roughly a full one-line header width (~120px) so it wraps only twice, while the seven data columns are squeezed to three-line headers. Width goes where the content is smallest (two-digit IDs) and is taken from the columns that actually hold text, leaving an uneven, front-heavy rhythm.

C.why: Essentially the balanced even-width solution: uniform three-line headers, equal rhythm across all eight columns, no clipped values and no orphaned characters. Header and body widths feel coherent; nothing draws the eye to a single misproportioned column.

D.why: Uniform but too narrow: headers are forced into four to five lines, so the header block is visibly taller and heavier than the data rows beneath it and starts to dominate the table. Still legible and unbroken, but the header/body balance is off and vertical scanning is slowed.

E.why: Widths are allocated unevenly, so some headers take three lines (日志留/存天数/达标) while others take four (系统/账户/口令/强度, 外部/网络/访问/开放). The ragged wrap heights destroy the header band, and the columns no longer read as a set of peers.

F.why: Balanced with a touch more room on the identifier columns, giving a uniform three-line header band, even column rhythm and comfortable numeric cells. Rows read as units and no word or number is broken.

reviews.unsure: A, C and F look very close in the renders; I may be reading sub-pixel width differences as design intent. If they are in fact identical, they should share the same grade, and C would join the best set.

A.why: First column is squeezed so the row header breaks into three cramped lines and several headers (e.g. 系统账户口令强度) stack into four short lines; the header band becomes a tall wall of fragments that is slow to scan, and column roles are hard to read at a glance.

B.why: Nearly equal widths keep the grid regular and the body reads cleanly, but the first column is too narrow for 受检服务器唯一编号 (three-line wrap) and several headers sit at two-to-three lines, so the header hierarchy looks slightly uneven.

C.why: The identifier column is given the extra width it needs (two clean lines), while the remaining columns are near-equal and every header wraps to a tidy two lines; the header band is uniform, rows read as units, and the whole table scans left-to-right naturally.

D.why: Similar to C with the row-header column clearly favoured and the last column given enough room for 应急联系人确认情况 in two lines; header heights are consistent, proportion and rhythm across columns are calm, and no word fragments awkwardly.

E.why: Widths are pushed to the extremes: the last column breaks 应急联系人确认情况 into four stacked lines and the middle headers into three, creating a very tall, ragged header band that dominates the table and makes comparison across columns harder.

F.why: Balanced, near-equal widths give a regular grid and readable two-line headers throughout; the identifier column is adequate though not generously wider than the rest, so its role as row header is slightly less pronounced than in C or D.

reviews.unsure: The six layouts are visually very close at this scale; exact column widths cannot be measured from the images, so the ranking of B/F versus C/D rests on how many header lines wrap and how clearly the row-header column stands out.
